content.text:
**Foreign investor flows into the KOSPI (Korea Composite Stock Price Index) have been highly volatile in 2026**, with periods of massive net selling (often tens to hundreds of trillions of KRW) offset by strong rebounds, valuation gains from the index rally, and occasional heavy buying. Foreigners own roughly 30–39% of the KOSPI's market capitalization (historically around 30–38.9% in recent data), making their flows a major driver of price movements, especially in large-caps like Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.[[1]](https://seoulclosingbell.com/how-foreign-investor-flows-move-the-kospi/)

### Recent Weekly and Daily Trends (as of late August–early September 2026)
Weekly net flows on the KOSPI cash market (from Korea Exchange data via Seoul Closing Bell, updated through August 28, 2026) show significant swings:

- **Aug 24–28, 2026** (5 sessions): Foreigners were **net sellers of ₩8.32 trillion** (institutions sold ₩0.36T; individuals bought ₩0.63T).
- **Aug 17–21**: Net buyers of ₩0.84T.
- **Aug 10–14**: Strong net buying of ₩6.55T.
- Earlier weeks in July–August alternated between net selling (e.g., ₩5.90T the week of Aug 3–7) and modest buying.[[1]](https://seoulclosingbell.com/how-foreign-investor-flows-move-the-kospi/)

On a daily basis as of **September 2, 2026**, foreigners recorded a net sell of **₩1,917 billion** on the KOSPI (worsening from ₩497 billion net sell the prior day). This places the latest reading at about the 33rd percentile historically for the year-to-date period.[[2]](https://caelion.dev/en/indicators/kospi_foreign_net_buy/)

Earlier in the summer (late June–early July 2026), foreigners executed a sharp sell-off of roughly **₩28 trillion (~$19 billion)** over eight consecutive sessions, contributing to a steep KOSPI correction (including a -7.89% day with a sidecar triggered). They flipped back to net buying around July 8–9 amid a semiconductor rebound.[[1]](https://seoulclosingbell.com/how-foreign-investor-flows-move-the-kospi/)

### Year-to-Date and Quarterly Context (2026)
- **Q2 2026** saw record growth in foreign investment holdings due to a massive KOSPI rally (+67.8% in the quarter). Outstanding foreign investment in South Korea hit a record **$3.02 trillion** by end-June (up $891.2 billion quarter-over-quarter, the largest increase on record). Securities investment (largely stocks) rose to $2.33 trillion. This was driven by valuation gains rather than pure inflows.[[3]](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20260820003100320)
- Despite this, cumulative **net selling** has been heavy in parts of the year: Over ₩191.9 trillion net sold on KOSPI from Jan 1 through early July (including alternative platforms), far exceeding prior years. Similar large net sales were reported earlier (e.g., ₩40.7T by early March; over ₩96T in one period). The index still rose in many stretches because domestic institutions (e.g., National Pension Service) and retail investors absorbed the supply.[[4]](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202607092055112955)
- Foreign ownership ratios have fluctuated but hit multi-year highs at times (e.g., ~38.9% in May, 37.18% in January, up to 39.45% in one report), even during net selling periods, due to the rally lifting the value of existing holdings. U.S. investors have been major participants, alongside those from Ireland, the UK, and others.[[5]](https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/05/06/foreign-ownership-of-kospi-hits-6-year-high-on-global)

### Broader Patterns and Drivers
- **Positive phases**: Foreign buying has powered rallies, especially in semiconductors and AI-related stocks (e.g., net buying helped push KOSPI above 8,000 or toward 9,000+ levels in spring/early summer). Returns on top foreign-bought stocks have often outperformed the index.[[6]](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/others/20260612/foreign-investors-return-to-kospi-buying-powering-rally-above-8000)
- **Selling pressure**: Often linked to portfolio rebalancing, FX moves, global risk-off sentiment, or profit-taking after sharp gains. Heavy selling streaks (e.g., 24–25 straight days) have occurred but were sometimes reversed quickly.
- Foreign flows remain a key variable for KOSPI direction, alongside domestic buying and global factors like U.S. tech performance.[[4]](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202607092055112955)

For the most granular daily data across all KOSPI/KOSDAQ stocks and sectors, open-source datasets (updated daily) are available on GitHub.[[7]](https://github.com/james-brand/korea-market-data)

Data is preliminary and subject to revision; sources include Bank of Korea, Korea Exchange (KRX), Financial Supervisory Service, and market reports. Trends can shift rapidly with market conditions.
